Reading the numbers

Every value column is points per 100 offensive possessions, and positive is better. rTS, role and zTS are true-shooting percentage points. rZTOV in the row detail is turnovers per 100 plays above the workload allowance, so negative is better.

Scoring value is the production zTS chain: 2 × TSA/100 × (zTS + 4) / 100, then the fitted line −1.211295 + 0.800618 × that.

Sources

Role is observed from 2006 to 2026 and a calibrated play-by-play backcast from 1997 to 2005. Missing observed-era roles stay blank. Turnover lanes are observed from 2014, identical to the rZTOV explorer, and box-estimated before that. Each lane is priced by a rolling five-season fit of the net-continuation turnover RAPMs.

Playtype mix RAPM · research

How easy or hard the whole lineup's shot diet is while the player is on offense, including the player's own shots and teammates' shots. It uses a lineup ridge with a 550-day half-life over the feature season and the one before it, with each playtype priced at the previous season's league value. A negative value means harder shots, which is the iso-heavy-creator pattern.

It is descriptive only. It never enters the ranking or scoring security, and it is not zTS, VPM or a prior.

Lineup TOV · research

What lineup data says about the same turnovers. A two-season on-court ridge with a 550-day half-life measures how many fewer turnovers the lineup commits with the player on offense, split into the player's own turnovers, teammates' turnovers, and unassigned team turnovers such as shot-clock violations. Each piece is priced at one kept possession. It is shown beside the box turnover values, never added to them. Team turnovers are missing from 1997-2013 source data.
